events.body:
C1: The trip was driven on an off-route segment from 18:32 to 18:39 covering 3.32 km where the optimal route covers only 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km and reaching up to 1262 m from the optimal route; overall 10.9 km actual vs 7.9 km optimal (+3.0 km, +38%). This is an un-exempted route deviation under RD-1. [F3 F1] [RD-1]
C2: The rider never consented to the reroute: the only chat message is the driver's 18:28 question 'ok if I go round via Outram Road?', and the record contains no rider reply before the segment started at 18:32; the driver's post-trip statement that there was 'no objection' is a claim, not consent, and cannot cure the silence under RD-5 / G11. [F7 F8 F9 F3] [RD-5]
C3: No traffic justification exists for the deviation: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip (F12), and the two band-3 records (20–29 km/h, F10/F11) are neither on the replaced optimal-road evidence of a severe obstruction nor sufficient alone to exempt a segment under RD-4(b). [F12 F10 F11 F13] [RD-4]
C4: RydeTAXI is metered, so the extra kilometres entered the fare: the off-route segment's 2.21 un-exempted extra km, plus the residual matching difference, produce excess distance billed of $4.21 (3.0 km × $1.41/km), and the fare breakdown shows distance $15.33 for 10.9 km against a 7.9 km estimate. [F3 F1 F4 F6] [RD-2]
C5: The refund on the un-exempted segment is 2.21 km × $1.41/km = $3.12 (the per-km rate taken from fare.distance_fare $15.33 ÷ fare.distance_km 10.9 = $1.4064, rounded); the remaining ~0.79 km of the 3.0 km excess is the apportioned mapping residual and is not claimed. [F3 F4 F6 F1] [RD-2]
C6: No driver-side traffic excuse, no published extra-charge item and no app-recorded destination change appear, so no additional fee is justified; the only charges on the bill are base, distance, time and platform fee ($1.47), all computed on the inflated 10.9 km / 22.2 min inputs. [F6 F4 F2] [RD-2]

claims.assertion: The trip was driven on an off-route segment from 18:32 to 18:39 covering 3.32 km where the optimal route covers only 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km and reaching up to 1262 m from the optimal route; overall 10.9 km actual vs 7.9 km optimal (+3.0 km, +38%). This is an un-exempted route deviation under RD-1.

The rider never consented to the reroute: the only chat message is the driver's 18:28 question 'ok if I go round via Outram Road?', and the record contains no rider reply before the segment started at 18:32; the driver's post-trip statement that there was 'no objection' is a claim, not consent, and cannot cure the silence under RD-5 / G11.

No traffic justification exists for the deviation: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip (F12), and the two band-3 records (20–29 km/h, F10/F11) are neither on the replaced optimal-road evidence of a severe obstruction nor sufficient alone to exempt a segment under RD-4(b).

RydeTAXI is metered, so the extra kilometres entered the fare: the off-route segment's 2.21 un-exempted extra km, plus the residual matching difference, produce excess distance billed of $4.21 (3.0 km × $1.41/km), and the fare breakdown shows distance $15.33 for 10.9 km against a 7.9 km estimate.

The refund on the un-exempted segment is 2.21 km × $1.41/km = $3.12 (the per-km rate taken from fare.distance_fare $15.33 ÷ fare.distance_km 10.9 = $1.4064, rounded); the remaining ~0.79 km of the 3.0 km excess is the apportioned mapping residual and is not claimed.

No driver-side traffic excuse, no published extra-charge item and no app-recorded destination change appear, so no additional fee is justified; the only charges on the bill are base, distance, time and platform fee ($1.47), all computed on the inflated 10.9 km / 22.2 min inputs.

weaknesses: The rider's silence after the driver's 18:28 message (F7, F8) can be read by the other side as acquiescence; RD-5 requires the rider's own message before the segment start, and a judge reading the bare question may be tempted to treat no-objection as agreement (the driver's F9 statement presses exactly this).

The driver will argue traffic cause: F10 (New Bridge Road band 3) and F11 (Sentosa Gateway band 3) show moderate congestion inside the trip window, and the driver's message names 'Kampong Bahru Road' — though F12 shows no recorded incident near the route, and RD-4(b) alone does not exempt a segment.

The refund formula (extra_km × per-km rate, RD-2) is not published by Ryde (G5) and the assumed rate comes from fare facts; the alternative 26¢/400 m meter structure (G10) would yield a different figure, so the amount is contestable.
F14 shows the rider has 2 disputes in 90 d with 0 upheld, which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of complaints; profile facts cannot decide the case but may colour it.

claims.assertion: The only off-route segment on the record is a single segment 18:32–18:39 that added 2.21 km over the optimal route's 1.10 km (F3); the total +3.0 km / +38% over 7.9 km (F1) is largely made up of that one segment, so the deviation to be judged is 18:32–18:39 and nothing else.

The segment is at least justified by traffic: the alternative corridor via Outram Road was chosen because congestion was building on Kampong Bahru Road (F7), and the traffic record for the trip window (18:14–18:54) shows speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway with no incidents recorded (F10, F11, F12), i.e. slow-moving roads around the route, with fair weather and no rain (F13).

The driver did not act unilaterally: 41 seconds after pickup he told the rider he intended to go round via Outram Road (F7 at 18:28), and the chat record is complete and every message timestamped (F8), so there is no evidence of any refusal or objection from the rider before the segment began at 18:32 (F3).

The driver's own written statement ('no objection, so I took it', F9) is not relied on as consent; the driver's case rests only on the absence of any rider message objecting, the completeness of the chat record (F8) and the traffic conditions (F10–F12).

No safety escalation is triggered: nothing in the chat (F7), the driver statement (F9) or the record reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, and no incident was recorded during the trip (F12).

If the court nevertheless treats the segment as unexcused, the metered excess is $4.21 (3.0 km × $1.41/km, F4) and in any event the deviation is attenuated by the fact that the driver has 752 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld route disputes (F15), so no account flag under RD-6 is warranted (F15).

weaknesses: The rider's complaint states 'he asked about another road but I did not reply; he went anyway' — the chat shows exactly that: a single driver message at 18:28 (F7) with no rider reply, and the segment started 18:32 (F3). Silence is not the rider's agreement under RD-5, so the other side will argue the 2.21 km extra_km segment was never consented to.

The driver's written statement that the rider gave 'no objection' (F9) is a claim, not consent (G11), and it is contradicted by the rider's account, so it will be discarded — the driver has no rider-side message approving the Outram Road routing.

The traffic evidence is weak on its face: no traffic incident was recorded at all (F12), so there is no RD-4(a) incident at all, and the only bands on record are band 3 (20–29 km/h, F10, F11) which is neither band 1 nor band 2, and in any event a band alone cannot ground an exemption under RD-4(b).

The chat message names Outram Road (F7), but the record shows no congestion data for Kampong Bahru Road itself (only New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway appear, F10, F11), so the stated reason is not corroborated on the replaced stretch of the optimal route as RD-4 requires.

The metered fare is distance- and time-based (F6: distance $15.33 on 10.9 km, time $5.76 on 22.2 min), so the 2.21 km deviation flows straight into an excess of $4.21 (F4) — the rider has a quantified, computable refund if the segment is unexcused.

points.response: Accepted as to the segment boundary: the judgeable deviation is the 18:32–18:39 off-route segment, and the 0.79 km difference between that segment's 2.21 km extra and the 3.0 km total excess is the map-matching residual that RD-2 says is not refunded — which is why we claim only $3.12.

RD-4 requires the traffic evidence to support the replaced stretch of the optimal route, and the only records produced are band 3 on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway (F10, F11) — neither on the replaced Kamong Bahru Road stretch the driver named (F7) — with no incident anywhere near the route (F12); band 3 is in any case not band 1 or 2 and, per RD-4(b), a band alone never exempts a segment.

A question is not consent: the only rider-side fact in the record is that there is no rider message at all before the segment started (F7 at 18:28, F3 segment start 18:32), and RD-5 requires the rider's own agreeing message to predate the segment start — the completeness of the record (F8) proves the absence, it does not supply the consent.

We accept the driver does not rely on F9, which confirms there is no record of consent at all — with no rider message before 18:32 (F7, F8, F3), the segment is unexempted under RD-5 regardless of the traffic data (F10–F12).
We do not allege any safety event, and we agree nothing in F7, F9 or F12 triggers SAFE-1 or SAFE-2; no escalation is sought.

On the merits the metered excess is exactly the $4.21 the driver state(fixed) — distance $15.33 on 10.9 km against a 7.9 km estimate (F4, F6, F1) — and RD-2's formula yields 2.21 km × $1.41/km ≈ $3.12 for the unexempted segment; our brief requested only refund_partial, not a flag_account, and we do not press RD-6.

The 2.21 km / 18:32–18:39 segment is correctly identified (F3), but 'un-exempted' is the conclusion in dispute and the +38% headline overstates it: the segment is one continuous stretch and the trip ran 22.2 min against a 16 min estimate (F2), consistent with a driver routing around slow roads rather than taking a detour for its own sake.

We do not rest on consent: we accept silence is not agreement under RD-5, but the only chat message is the driver's 18:28 notice (F7) and the record is complete and timestamped (F8), so there is no rider message refusing the Outram Road routing at any point before 18:32 (F3).

RD-4 does not require an incident to exist where none does; the driver's contemporaneous reason was congestion building on Kampong Bahru Road (F7), and the trip-window records show band 3 (20–29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway (F10, F11) with no incident and fair weather (F12, F13), i.e. a slow evening corridor — the segment should be treated as reasonably caused rather than penalised.

The fare mechanics are not disputed — the trip was metered and distance is billed per km (F6) — but the $4.21 figure is the whole 3.0 km deviation (F4), whereas the segment actually attributed to off-route driving is 2.21 km (F3), the rest being residual matching difference.

If the court finds the segment unexcused, the arithmetic is accepted at 2.21 km × $1.41/km ≈ $3.12 (F3, F4, F6) — but that is a maximum, not a floor, and it is only payable if the RD-4 traffic explanation fails.

Correct that no extra published item was charged: the bill is base, distance, time and platform fee only with $0.00 waiting and non-published surcharges (F6, F5), which shows the driver took no waiting fee, no destination-change fee and added nothing manual — the deviation, if any, is a routing matter only.

We withdraw nothing but clarify: our no_action request rests on the traffic explanation (F7, F10–F12); if it fails, $3.12 is the correct ceiling and the 752-trip, 0-upheld record (F15) means no RD-6 flag is warranted.
